description: Operator-invoked recovery input for the employment lifecycle actuator epic — worker classification, jurisdiction, and employment events as Workroom definitions.

epic.title: Employment lifecycle actuator: make an employment event do the work
epic.description:
## Problem

DPF's workforce spine holds 58 models covering hiring, onboarding checklists, time, leave, reviews, pay runs and terminations. `EmploymentEvent` records every lifecycle transition against a closed 16-value type union and a validated `LIFECYCLE_TRANSITION_MATRIX`. Nothing subscribes to it. Verified 2026-08-25: the only consumers of `EmploymentEvent` are `apps/web/lib/actions/workforce.ts`, `workforce-types.ts`, `people-supplier-configs.ts`, `legacy-coverage-baseline.ts` and `table-classification.ts` — all read/write/display. It is a log, not a trigger.

The consequence is that hiring a person produces a record and a checklist, and no account, group, licence, device, payroll enrolment or access grant. Terminating a person produces a `TerminationRecord` and revokes nothing. Benchmarking against Rippling (see the design's Research section) shows this — not record breadth — is the capability its users name as the thing they love.

Three business nuances make a naive actuator unsafe rather than merely incomplete:

1. **Worker classification.** `EmploymentType.name` is free text with no legal semantics. There is no model of employee vs direct contractor vs agency contractor vs EOR vs volunteer. Verified: zero occurrences of co-employment, misclassification or contingent-worker vocabulary anywhere in the tree.
2. **Co-employment.** Directing and controlling a contingent worker the way an employee is directed is the factual test that creates joint-employer liability. An actuator that provisions and assigns identically for every worker manufactures that evidence automatically, at scale, with a timestamped audit trail.
3. **Jurisdiction.** `Organization.employsIn` already declares where staff work and the schema comment already states employment law keys off that dimension, but no worker resolves to a jurisdiction: `WorkLocation` carries an address and timezone and no jurisdiction slug.

## Outcome

An employment event spawns a governed Workroom instance from a versioned Workroom definition, whose steps are classification-aware and jurisdiction-scoped, and whose provisioning actions resolve to connector capabilities. Referrals become an evidenced relationship rather than a source label.

## Grounding

Extends, does not duplicate:

- `WORK_CASE_SOURCE_REGISTRY` (`apps/web/lib/work-management/source-registry.ts`) — 13 source keys, none for workforce.
- The Workroom definition/occurrence boundary shipped under BI-80BECE1E (`docs/architecture/workroom-vocabulary-boundary.md`). Definitions already declare trigger classes, authority, review, escalation, completion rules and event-triggered spawn rules. No new engine is required.
- `RegulatoryAutonomyPolicy` and `JurisdictionCriteriaProfile`, both keyed on (industry, jurisdiction, jurisdictionBasis, activityClass) — the jurisdictional gate already exists and needs new activity classes, not a new policy spine.
- `apps/web/lib/workforce/approval-routing.ts` (BI-HCM-004) — the accountable-approver chain walk, already fail-loud.
- `ProtectedMonitoringObservation` — the structurally separated adverse-impact rail for hiring.
- EP-24741BBF (Directory Service) supplies the provisioning target; this epic consumes it and must not fork it.

## Boundary

The platform never determines a worker's classification. It makes the determination explicit, jurisdiction-scoped, evidenced and consequential, and refuses actions that contradict a recorded classification. Classification is a customer business decision and routes through the WWWD Decision Perspective Gate, never `principle_decide`. This mirrors the standing payroll boundary: prepare the artifact, never move the money.
epic.scopeRationale: Every archetype engages workers — employees, contractors, volunteers — and the joiner/mover/leaver shape plus its approval authority is universal. Jurisdictional employment rules are per-organization data over a universal policy spine, not per-archetype logic.

items.title: Spawn Workroom instances from employment events
items.body:
## Problem

This is the item the epic exists for.

`EmploymentEvent` is written on every lifecycle transition, typed by a closed 16-value `EmploymentEventType` union and guarded by `LIFECYCLE_TRANSITION_MATRIX`, which validates every status move. The vocabulary and the state machine are already correct and already enforced.

Verified 2026-08-25: nothing subscribes. The only consumers are the workforce actions that write it, the type module that declares it, a workbook supplier config, a legacy coverage baseline and a table classification map. Hiring someone appends a row and creates checklist items that a human then works by hand.

The Workroom definition contract already provides for this: definitions declare trigger classes and event-triggered spawn rules. The trigger source and the definition both exist; the edge between them does not.

## Scope

Bind `EmploymentEventType` values to the definitions registered by BI-28EFA338, so a lifecycle transition spawns the governed Workroom instance its definition prescribes:

- `hired`, `offer_accepted`, `onboarding_started` spawn `worker-onboarding`
- `manager_changed`, `department_changed`, `position_changed` spawn `worker-change`
- `offboarding_started`, `terminated` spawn `worker-offboarding`
- `leave_started`, `leave_ended`, `activated`, `reactivated` update an open instance rather than spawning a new one

Spawning is idempotent on (event, definition): replaying an event, or two writers racing the same transition, yields one instance. `Workroom.idempotencyKey` already carries a unique constraint and is the mechanism.

An event whose definition cannot be resolved, or whose worker has no resolvable classification or jurisdiction, does not spawn a partial instance. It surfaces as operator work naming the missing input. A half-provisioned worker is worse than an unprovisioned one.

## Acceptance criteria

- Each of the 16 `EmploymentEventType` values has an explicit disposition: spawns a named definition, updates an open instance, or is deliberately inert with a recorded reason. No value is unhandled by omission.
- Spawning is idempotent under event replay and under two concurrent writers of the same transition.
- An event for a worker with unresolved classification or jurisdiction produces operator work, never a partial instance.
- The spawned instance carries the subject worker, the originating event, the definition key and version, and the requesting principal.
- `LIFECYCLE_TRANSITION_MATRIX` remains the single authority on legal transitions; this item adds no second state machine.
- Tests cover replay, concurrent-writer, unresolved-input and inert-event paths.

## Dependencies

BI-28EFA338 (definitions), BI-C61CEEA9 (classification), BI-9252B9EA (jurisdiction). Provisioning actions inside the spawned instance are BI-828F8EC9.

items.title: Register the employment lifecycle as Workroom definitions in the source registry
items.body:
## Problem

`WORK_CASE_SOURCE_REGISTRY` holds 13 source definitions — `task-node`, `backlog-item`, `work-capsule`, `approval`, `data-control-operation`, `manual-task`, `scheduled`, `engagement`, `opportunity`, `booking`, `storefront-booking`, `activity`, `field-service-job`. None is a workforce shape.

BI-80BECE1E shipped the definition/occurrence seam through this exact registry: a definition owns a stable key, a positive version, a finite-or-standing mode and a decision scope, and `buildWorkroomView` projects definition identity alongside occurrence trace with repository, worktree and PR evidence optional. `docs/architecture/workroom-vocabulary-boundary.md` states the contract directly: no development evidence is required for an ordinary business instance, and later work must deepen this registry rather than create a parallel Workroom-definition surface.

The employment lifecycle is therefore a set of registry entries, not a new automation engine. Building a workflow engine beside this registry would be the parallel-surface defect the boundary document exists to prevent.

## Scope

Register the employment lifecycle definitions:

- `worker-onboarding` (joiner) — finite
- `worker-change` (mover) — finite
- `worker-offboarding` (leaver) — finite
- `worker-classification-review` — standing, periodic
- `referral-intake` — finite

Each entry declares what the definition contract already requires: intended outcome, trigger classes, finite-or-standing instance policy, owning decision scope, authority, review, escalation and completion rules, accountable and contributing roles without pre-assigning a person, required outcome-packet categories, and coordinated portfolio role.

All five sit at `defaultDecisionScope: "wwwd"` and `portfolioRole: "forEmployees"`. They are the customer's business decisions about their own workforce, not platform-development decisions — AGENTS.md section 11 forbids settling them through `principle_decide`.

Authority resolves through the existing `apps/web/lib/workforce/approval-routing.ts` chain walk rather than a second approver model; its fail-loud unresolved posture and transient `onBehalfOf` handling carry over unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

- Five definitions are registered in `WORK_CASE_SOURCE_REGISTRY` with stable keys and positive versions; no second registry, route, API or queue is added.
- Each definition declares its trigger classes, authority, review, escalation and completion rules per the definition contract in `docs/architecture/workroom-vocabulary-boundary.md`.
- A workforce Workroom instance projects definition and occurrence identity with no repository, worktree, branch, PR or CI evidence present, and loses no identity by their absence.
- The Workspace surface renders a workforce instance business-first on Overview, with Details disclosing activity, participants, evidence and receipts — the disclosure contract AC-WR-004 established.
- Approvals inside these definitions resolve through `approval-routing.ts`; an unresolved chain surfaces as operator work with its reason.
- Contract tests fail before registration and pass after.

## Dependencies

Consumes the definition/occurrence seam from BI-80BECE1E. Does not extend the portable Work Packet program in BI-D4C110BC.

items.title: Resolve onboarding and offboarding steps to connector capabilities
items.body:
## Problem

A spawned onboarding Workroom instance can hold steps and assign them to people. It cannot yet create an account, assign a group, provision a mailbox or revoke access on a termination date, because nothing binds a lifecycle step to an executable capability.

The binding surface exists. `apps/web/lib/integrations/kernel/` defines a frozen connector contract with a dotted capability namespace, a capability-indexed registry that rejects duplicate capability keys at construction, an encrypted credential envelope, a typed error taxonomy and an audit trail with canonical argument hashing. Three connectors are registered on it today.

The identity target is being built under EP-24741BBF, which is closing the split between `User` as authentication root and `Principal` as authorization root. That epic owns the directory; this item consumes it and must not fork it.

Where no connector covers a capability an org needs, that gap is the on-demand integration case, not a reason to hand-build another bespoke connector.

## Scope

Make a lifecycle step address a capability rather than name a system. A step declares `directory.user.create` or `directory.group.assign`; the registry resolves which connector serves it, or reports that none does.

Revocation is date-bound. An offboarding step scheduled for a termination date executes on that date, and the instance stays open and accountable until it does. An unexecuted revocation is visible operator work, never a closed room.

Every step is classification-gated through BI-B506AD2E before it executes, so provisioning a contingent worker follows that worker's lawful path rather than the employee path.

An unresolved capability is an honest, actionable gap: it names the missing capability and opens the integration decision — absorb, generate a connector on demand, or record the step as manual — rather than failing anonymously.

## Acceptance criteria

- A lifecycle step declares a capability identifier; connector selection is by capability through the existing registry, never by a hardcoded connector key.
- An unresolved capability produces a named gap with the three dispositions available, not an anonymous failure.
- A dated revocation executes on its date; the instance cannot reach completion with an unexecuted revocation outstanding.
- Every provisioning and deprovisioning attempt writes a connector audit row through the existing audit path.
- No new credential storage is introduced; the kernel encrypted envelope is the only store.
- Classification gating runs before execution, proven by a test where the employee path executes and the contingent path refuses.
- Tests use the existing contract harness, exercising auth-failure, rate-limited, token-expired and malformed-response scenarios against the provisioning path.

## Dependencies

EP-24741BBF supplies the directory target. BI-B506AD2E supplies the gate. BI-2624B7EA supplies the instance. Connectors not yet on the kernel cannot serve capabilities; that migration is integration-strategy work tracked outside this epic.

items.title: Resolve every worker to an employment jurisdiction
items.body:
## Problem

`Organization` already declares employment jurisdiction: `employsIn String[]` holds PROFESSION_JURISDICTIONS slugs, and the schema comment states plainly that employment law keys off where staff work, distinct from where the business sells or operates. That declaration reaches nothing. `WorkLocation` carries a name, a `locationType`, a timezone and an optional `Address`, and no jurisdiction. `EmployeeProfile` carries a `workLocationId` and a `timezone` string.

So the org knows it employs in three jurisdictions and cannot say which one governs any individual worker. Every jurisdiction-scoped rule in EP-862820FD — classification tests, leave entitlement, notice periods, what an offboarding may lawfully revoke and when — has no key to look up.

`RegulatoryAutonomyPolicy` and `JurisdictionCriteriaProfile` are both already keyed on (industry, jurisdiction, jurisdictionBasis, activityClass). The lookup spine exists. The worker cannot supply the key.

## Scope

Give `WorkLocation` a jurisdiction, and add the resolver that answers "which employment jurisdiction governs this worker" from the work location, falling back explicitly and never silently.

Jurisdiction is multi-dimensional and this item claims exactly one dimension: the employment basis. Sales-tax, data-residency and marketing-consent bases already resolve from their own `Organization` columns and are untouched.

A worker whose jurisdiction cannot be resolved is surfaced as operator work with the reason, in the same fail-loud posture as `approval-routing.ts` — never defaulted to `global` behind the operator's back, because a silent default here produces a confidently wrong legal answer.

## Acceptance criteria

- `WorkLocation` carries a jurisdiction slug validated against the same PROFESSION_JURISDICTIONS vocabulary `Organization.employsIn` uses.
- A resolver returns the governing employment jurisdiction for a worker, or an explicit unresolved result naming the reason (no work location, location without jurisdiction, jurisdiction not in the org `employsIn` set).
- An unresolved jurisdiction is operator-visible work, not a `global` fallback.
- Where a location jurisdiction is absent from `Organization.employsIn`, that contradiction is reported rather than reconciled.
- The resolved jurisdiction is accepted directly as the `jurisdiction` key by `RegulatoryAutonomyPolicy` and `JurisdictionCriteriaProfile` lookups; no translation layer is introduced.
- Migration applies cleanly against populated data; existing locations become explicitly unresolved rather than being assigned a guess.
- Unit tests cover each unresolved reason and the org/location contradiction case.

## Out of scope

Seeding jurisdictional employment rule content. Any change to the tax jurisdiction reference model in `finance.prisma`, which is a separate basis.

items.title: Refuse actions that contradict a worker classification (co-employment control)
items.body:
## Problem

Joint-employer and misclassification liability turns on conduct, not paperwork. The tests regulators apply — behavioural control, financial control, integration into the organisation, permanence — are satisfied by what a system records the org actually doing to a worker.

An actuator that treats every worker identically is therefore not merely legally naive. It industrialises the evidence: it assigns mandatory training to a contractor, puts an agency temp into a performance review cycle, schedules a volunteer into a rostered shift, and timestamps all of it in an auditable ledger the org later hands to an investigator.

This risk arrives with the actuator and must land in the same epic, not after it.

## Scope

Make classification consequential at the point of action. A Workroom step that would direct, schedule, review or integrate a worker checks the worker classification and the resolved jurisdiction before it runs, and refuses where the combination is unlawful or unsafe.

The check routes through the existing policy spine, not a new one. `RegulatoryAutonomyPolicy` is already keyed on (industry, jurisdiction, jurisdictionBasis, activityClass) and already carries `maxAutonomyLevel`, `humanControlRequired` and `requiredEvidence`. This item adds the activity classes — `worker-direction`, `worker-classification`, `worker-provisioning` — and the seeded policy rows behind them.

A refusal is a stop, not a workaround (AGENTS.md section 1). It names the classification, the jurisdiction, the rule and the lawful alternative — a contractor is not assigned mandatory training, they are sent a statement of work amendment — so the operator can act rather than route around it.

The classification determination itself routes through the WWWD Decision Perspective Gate. The platform presents the factors, records the human determination and holds the evidence. It never decides. Misclassification liability sits with the employer, and a platform asserting a classification would be both outside its authority and wrong to.

## Acceptance criteria

- Direction, scheduling, review-cycle enrolment and mandatory-training assignment each check classification plus jurisdiction before executing.
- Refusals are typed, name the governing rule, and state the lawful alternative; they never silently no-op or degrade to a warning.
- New activity classes are added to the existing `RegulatoryAutonomyPolicy` spine; no parallel policy model is introduced.
- A classification determination carries a human author and evidence; no code path derives one.
- The `worker-classification-review` standing definition surfaces a determination for periodic re-confirmation when the facts of engagement drift — duration extended, direction increased, exclusivity emerged.
- Tests cover a refusal per classification and a jurisdiction where the same action is permitted, proving the check reads jurisdiction and not just classification.

## Dependencies

BI-C61CEEA9 (classification), BI-9252B9EA (jurisdiction), BI-28EFA338 (definitions). Related but not blocked by BI-514826D3, the deferred policy-authority bridge; this item uses the existing policy read path and must not fork it.

items.title: Model worker classification as a typed axis with legal consequence
items.body:
## Problem

`EmploymentType` is a free-text name table (`name String`, `status String`) with no legal semantics. "Contractor", "Full-time" and "Volunteer" are labels an org types in. Nothing downstream can ask the only question that matters — may this worker be directed, scheduled, reviewed and provisioned the way an employee is? — because the answer is not represented.

Verified 2026-08-25: no co-employment, misclassification, contingent-worker or equivalent vocabulary exists anywhere in `apps/web/lib`, `packages/db` or `docs`.

This blocks every other item in EP-862820FD. An actuator that provisions without reading a classification is not a smaller version of the right thing; it is the mechanism that manufactures joint-employer evidence.

## Scope

Add `WorkerClassification` as a typed, closed enum (AGENTS.md section 8: closed-set string fields are Prisma enums plus a generated TypeScript union, never free-form strings), distinct from the org's `EmploymentType` label:

`employee`, `contractor-direct`, `contractor-agency`, `temp-agency-worker`, `eor-employee`, `volunteer`, `intern`, `board-member`.

Each classification declares typed consequences, not prose: whether payroll withholding applies, whether the worker may be directed and scheduled by the org, whether they accrue leave and benefits, whether they enter performance review cycles, and whether they appear in the org chart as a reporting line or as an engaged party.

`EmploymentType` is retained as the org's own display label and gains a required classification reference, so an existing installation's labels are mapped rather than replaced.

The engagement term is modelled here too: a contingent worker has a definite end date and an engagement that can be extended, which is a different fact from an employee `endDate`.

## Acceptance criteria

- `WorkerClassification` is a Prisma enum with a generated TypeScript union; no consumer reads a free-form classification string.
- Every `EmploymentType` row resolves to exactly one classification; the migration maps existing rows and applies cleanly against a populated database.
- Classification consequences are queryable as typed values, not inferred from label text.
- A contingent engagement carries a definite term and an extension history distinguishable from employee `endDate`.
- The platform records a classification determination with its author and evidence; it never derives or asserts one. A determination with no recorded human author is invalid.
- Unit tests cover each classification consequence set and the migration mapping of pre-existing labels.

## Out of scope

Refusing actions on the basis of classification (the co-employment control item). Jurisdiction resolution (its own item). Any change to payroll calculation.

items.title: Make an employee referral an evidenced relationship, not a source label
items.body:
## Problem

`RecruitingSource.type` accepts `referral` as one of five category labels. `Candidate.sourceId` points at that row. Nothing records who referred whom.

So the platform can report how many hires came through referrals and cannot answer any question that follows from it: who is owed a referral bonus and when it vests, whether the referrer sat in the approval chain for their own referral, or whether referral hiring is narrowing the workforce.

That last one is not a reporting nicety. Referral pipelines reproduce the existing shape of a workforce, which is the textbook adverse-impact risk in hiring. DPF already carries the rail built for exactly this: `ProtectedMonitoringObservation` is deliberately structurally separate from the scoring path, joined to an evaluation only by an opaque `evaluationRef`, and exists to compute four-fifths and NYC LL144 impact ratios. It is unused for referral analysis because referrals are not represented.

## Scope

Add the referrer relationship, and the three consequences that follow from having it.

**Attribution.** An application records the referring worker, distinct from the recruiting source category. A referral by a contingent worker is attributable but does not imply the referrer may participate in hiring decisions.

**Conflict of interest.** The referrer is excluded from the approval chain for their own referral. `apps/web/lib/workforce/approval-routing.ts` already walks the chain and already skips hops that cannot act, with typed skip reasons. This adds one skip reason and reuses the walk; it does not fork it. The chain-exhausted and reporting-loop cases already fail loud and continue to.

**Bonus.** A referral bonus is a tenure-gated payroll consequence, not an ad-hoc payment. It is a `referral-intake` Workroom instance that stays open to its vesting milestone and then produces a pay component line. It never moves money — the standing payroll boundary is unchanged.

**Monitoring.** Referral-sourced outcomes feed `ProtectedMonitoringObservation` through its existing opaque correlation, where collection is lawful and consented. The structural separation is preserved exactly: the referral relationship must never become a scoring input, and must not share a foreign key with one.

## Acceptance criteria

- An application records its referring worker; a referral without a resolvable referrer is rejected rather than stored as an orphan.
- The referrer cannot appear as an approver on their own referral; the exclusion is a skip reason in the existing chain walk, not a second routing implementation.
- A referral bonus vests against a tenure milestone and emits a pay component line; it initiates no payment.
- Referral-sourced outcomes reach `ProtectedMonitoringObservation` only through the existing opaque `evaluationRef`, with no foreign key to any scoring model, and only where a consent basis is recorded.
- Tests cover the self-approval exclusion, the orphan-referrer rejection, and the absence of any scoring-path relation from the referral record.

## Dependencies

BI-28EFA338 for the `referral-intake` definition. Classification (BI-C61CEEA9) for the contingent-referrer case.
